records.title: bb
records.summary: A local server and app that runs Claude Code, Codex and other agent CLIs as threads. Its builtin automations plugin fires an agent prompt or a stored script on a 5-field cron with a timezone, or once at a set time or delay.
records.why_it_matters: The closest fit found for a single developer who wants a scheduled Claude Code or Codex run on their own Mac, with run history and a sidebar to pause or re-run it.
records.fit_notes: Free to run locally; agent runs bill to the provider you already pay for. The scheduler lives inside the bb server, so the Mac must be awake (the Keep Awake plugin runs caffeinate but a closed lid still sleeps). Automations have no approval step of their own: an omitted --permission-mode falls back to auto, or to Full Access when the provider lacks auto. Telemetry to PostHog is on in production runs until you set BB_TELEMETRY=false. A code read (plugins/automations/src/rpc-types.ts, data.ts) shows script variables from --env-json kept as a string map inside the execution JSON in the plugin's SQLite file, so do not pass API keys that way; the docs do not say this. Not checked: missed-tick behaviour after sleep (the code computes the next run from the current time, which suggests missed ticks collapse into one run, but no doc states it).

claims.text: A schedule is a 5-field cron expression with an IANA timezone, or a one-shot time or delay.
claims.quote:
--cron <expr>                  Recurring 5-field cron expression
--timezone <tz>                IANA timezone for --cron
--at <datetime>                One-shot run time, preferably ISO 8601
--in <duration>                One-shot delay, e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d

claims.text: With no permission mode set, an agent automation runs in auto approval, or in Full Access when the provider has no auto mode.
claims.quote:
When `--permission-mode` is omitted, the plugin chooses Approve for me
(`auto`) when the provider supports it and otherwise uses Full Access
(`full`).

claims.text: Production runs send anonymous usage telemetry by default; BB_TELEMETRY=false turns it off.
claims.quote:
Production runs (the desktop app, `npx bb-app`, and `pnpm start` checkouts) send
anonymous usage telemetry

records.title: Hermes Agent
records.summary: Nous Research's self-hosted agent with its own model routing, skills, messaging gateways and a cron scheduler that runs agent or script jobs.
records.why_it_matters: It is a full agent, not a wrapper for Claude Code, and its cron plus chat approvals is the most complete unattended loop with a human answer step found in this lane.
records.fit_notes: Agent jobs need a model provider key, a subscription provider or the Nous Portal (script-only jobs use no model); it does not drive your Claude Code subscription. Jobs live in ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json and secrets in the owning profile's .env or an external secret source. Dangerous commands in cron are denied by default (see the security source). The plugin catalog lists third-party plugins, including one that opens an unauthenticated local dashboard; read a plugin before enabling it. Telemetry default not found in README or the pages read.

claims.text: The scheduler runs inside the gateway daemon, which ticks every 60 seconds; the gateway can be installed as a user or system service.
claims.quote: **Cron execution is handled by the gateway daemon.** The gateway ticks the scheduler every 60 seconds, running any due jobs in isolated agent sessions.

claims.text: By default a missed cron occurrence runs late only inside a catch-up window of half the period, clamped to 2 minutes - 2 hours; --grace-minutes or --catch-up on change this per job.
claims.quote: A missed cron occurrence is run late only inside a catch-up window: half the job's period, clamped to 2 minutes–2 hours.

claims.text: A job can be created paused with a reason and resumed by a person, which serves as a review gate before the first fire.
claims.quote: Omit the reason to store "Created paused; awaiting operator approval."
claims.locator: section Creating a job paused (safe canary)

records.title: Kanban Video Pipeline
records.summary: A Hermes Agent demo in which director, cinematographer, renderer and editor profiles split a brief into a task graph and produce an MP4 with ASCII video, p5.js and ffmpeg.
records.why_it_matters: A worked example of an agent video pipeline driven by a task board instead of a person, with a block-and-notify path when something fails.
records.fit_notes: Needs Hermes, a running gateway and an OpenRouter key (the README names claude-opus-4.6), so every run is paid. No approval step before the final cut: a person steps in when a worker blocks, or by choice to nudge, skip to the editor or re-render a scene. The setup sources ~/.hermes/.env into the shell. It is built around one demo video, with README steps to adapt it to your own brief; setup.sh was not run or read in full.

claims.text: The pipeline runs with no human input; stages promote when their parents complete.
claims.quote: The entire pipeline auto-runs with zero human intervention.

claims.text: The gateway hosts the board dispatcher, which picks up ready tasks every 60 seconds; tasks stuck in "ready" mean the gateway is not running.
claims.quote: The gateway hosts the kanban dispatcher that picks up ready tasks every 60 seconds.
claims.locator: RUN.md, step 2 Gateway must be running

claims.text: A blocked worker notifies you, and unblocking respawns it with your comment in context.
claims.quote: Unblock (respawns the worker with your comment in context)

records.title: n8n
records.summary: A self-hostable visual workflow engine with schedule triggers, AI agent nodes and a human review step for agent tool calls.
records.why_it_matters: Self-hosted n8n gives a single developer a scheduler plus a Slack or Telegram approval before an agent tool runs, for example before a publish.
records.fit_notes: Licence gotcha: the Sustainable Use License allows internal business, non-commercial or personal use, so selling n8n as a hosted service to clients is out; files with .ee. need an enterprise licence. Self-hosted telemetry is on until N8N_DIAGNOSTICS_ENABLED=false. Needs Docker or Node and a machine that stays on. It does not run Claude Code itself; call claude -p from an Execute Command node or use its own AI nodes. Schedule trigger docs were not read.

claims.text: Its Sustainable Use License limits use to internal business, non-commercial or personal purposes.
claims.quote:
You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or
personal use.

claims.text: A tool that needs human review pauses the workflow and sends an approval request through a channel such as Slack or Telegram.
claims.quote: The workflow pauses and sends an approval request through your configured channel (such as Slack, Telegram, or the n8n Chat interface).
claims.locator: docs human-in-the-loop-for-tools, How it works, step 2

claims.text: Self-hosted n8n collects telemetry by default.
claims.quote: n8n enables telemetry collection by default.
claims.locator: docs control-telemetry, Opting out of data collection

records.title: Activepieces
records.summary: A self-hostable no-code automation builder, MIT-licensed outside its enterprise folders.
records.why_it_matters: A permissive alternative to n8n, but its documented approval feature gates publishing a flow, not a step inside a run.
records.fit_notes: Flow Approvals is an Enterprise or Cloud feature and reviews flow changes before they go live; it is not a run-time human step. Product analytics and a daily deployment snapshot are on until switched off. Run-time approval pieces and schedule triggers were not read.

claims.text: Code outside the enterprise directories is MIT (Expat) licensed.
claims.quote: Content outside of the above mentioned directories or restrictions above is available under the "MIT Expat" license as defined below.

claims.text: Flow Approvals is an Enterprise or Cloud feature that holds a flow offline until an approver reviews it.
claims.quote: Flow Approvals is an Enterprise / Cloud feature and requires the Environments plan.

claims.text: The daily deployment snapshot is on by default and ignores AP_TELEMETRY_ENABLED.
claims.quote: **Deployment setup** is a separate switch in the same place, and is on by default.

checked.what: LICENSE, flow-approvals.mdx and telemetry.mdx from the repo against the claims

records.title: Windmill
records.summary: A self-hostable engine for scripts, flows and schedules, with approval steps that suspend a flow until a person resumes it.
records.why_it_matters: Its suspend-until-approval step is a run-time human gate in the free edition, which fits a 'render, then wait for my OK, then publish' flow.
records.fit_notes: Licence gotcha: the Community Edition is free to use internally but may not be sold, resold or run as a managed service without an agreement; a source build without the "enterprise" feature flag is AGPLv3. Approval works through secret resume URLs, so unless the step requires logged-in approvers or group membership, anyone who gets the URL can approve; send it only to the approver. Telemetry default and schedule docs were not read.

claims.text: The Community Edition may be used free and redistributed as is, but not sold, served as a managed service or wrapped without an agreement.
claims.quote:
but not to sell, resell, serve as a managed service, modify or wrap under any
form without an explicit agreement.

claims.text: An approval step suspends the flow until it is approved through resume endpoints or the approval page, only by holders of the secret URLs.
claims.quote: This will suspend the execution of a flow until it has been approved through the resume endpoints or the approval page by and solely by the recipients of the secret URLs.

records.title: Trigger.dev
records.summary: A TypeScript background-job platform, hosted or self-hosted, with cron-scheduled tasks and waitpoint tokens that pause a run until completed.
records.why_it_matters: Waitpoint tokens give code-first approval: a render task waits for an 'approved' or 'rejected' payload before it publishes.
records.fit_notes: Self-hosting lacks checkpoints, so a waiting run holds its resources instead of sleeping; long approval waits cost more there. Declarative schedules apply only after a dev or deploy command. Telemetry default of the self-hosted build was not checked.

claims.text: Waitpoint tokens pause a run until completed and are meant for approval and human-in-the-loop steps.
claims.quote: Waitpoint tokens pause task runs until you complete the token. They're commonly used for approval workflows

claims.text: Declarative schedules live on the task and sync when you run the dev command or deploy.
claims.quote: They sync when you run the dev command or deploy.

claims.text: Checkpoints (non-blocking waits) are Cloud-only; self-hosted runs do not get them.
claims.quote: | Checkpoints       | ✅    | ❌          | Non-blocking waits, less resource usage |

checked.what: three docs files from the repo against the claims

records.title: Temporal
records.summary: A durable-execution server; Schedules start workflow executions on calendar or interval specs, with overlap and catch-up policies.
records.why_it_matters: The heaviest option here, but the one with explicit, documented rules for overlapping and late runs.
records.fit_notes: Needs a Temporal server plus your own workers, which is a lot for one developer making clips. There is no approval primitive in the schedule doc; a human step means writing a signal handler. The default one-year catch-up window means a server down for a week fires the backlog per the overlap policy when it returns. Licence was not quoted and telemetry was not checked.

claims.text: By default a scheduled start is skipped when the previous execution is still running.
claims.quote:
- `Skip`: **Default**.
  Nothing happens; the Workflow Execution is not started.

claims.text: The default catch-up window is one year, so late actions still run unless over a year late.
claims.quote: The default is one year, meaning Actions will be taken unless over one year late.
